title: Change evaluation: CR-014 team chat notification channel

change.title: Team chat notification channel
change.description: Adds a fifth notification channel: messages to an agency's team chat channel through a chat messaging service run by another company (T6). Notification workers (P2) gain an outbound HTTPS connection to it. Messages carry an alert reference ID and fixed text only (PF3). Agency administrators turn the channel on and add chat channel addresses to escalation rules; addresses are stored with the routing policy (D2).

timeline.business_days: Monday to Friday, skipping US federal holidays on their observed dates (5 U.S.C. 6103) (FedRAMP does not define business days; confirm with the consultant)
timeline.note: Read SCN-TRF-TPR (third-party review before starting) and SCN-CSO-INF (required content).

inputs.description: Change request CR-014: team chat notification channel
Scope change log, SC-001 and SC-002

items.question: Is the change likely to substantively affect the security posture? (FRD-SGC)
items.answer: Yes. It adds a third-party service in the alert delivery path (T6), a new outbound flow from the notification workers (P2), and a new kind of address stored with the routing policy (D2). Each of these changes the scope record.

items.question: Is it likely to change the certification class? (FRD-CCC)
items.answer: No. The request adds no new data class and describes no change to impact levels.

items.question: Does it recur routinely as part of ongoing operations? (FRD-RTR)
items.answer: No. It is the first chat channel, and the change log has no earlier change of this kind.

items.question: Does it introduce substantive risks that must be assessed in depth? (FRD-TRF)
items.answer: Proposed yes, for the SME to confirm. The change adds a capability agencies configure and use, and a new third party that needs the MAS-CSO-TPR documentation. Against that, messages follow the existing payload policy (PF3), which could make it adaptive if the SME judges that existing checks verify it with minor changes. See DQ-001.

items.item: Significant Change type and explanation of categorization
items.supplied: Yes, once DQ-001 is decided: EV-1 to EV-4

items.item: Summary of customer impact, including changes to services and customer configuration responsibilities
items.supplied: Partly: agency administrators turn the channel on and add addresses; who is responsible for the chat channel's own settings is not stated

items.item: Plan and timeline for the change, including for the verification, assessment, and/or validation of impacted Key Security Indicators or Rev5 Controls
items.supplied: Partly: dates and testing are stated; the impacted KSIs are not identified

items.item: Copy of the business or security impact analysis

items.supplied: No: the requester is named, the approver is not

detail.id: SC-003 (draft, not yet in the log)
detail.summary: Team chat notification channel through a new third-party chat messaging service (T6), with a new outbound flow from P2 and chat channel addresses stored with the routing policy (D2).
detail.evaluation: EV-1 to EV-4 in this deliverable
detail.needs_before_entry: T6 entry with the MAS-CSO-TPR information (Q-004), new flow ID, consultant decision on the type

detail.requirement: CNA-7b, transformative: before the change starts, and again within 5 business days after it is finished
detail.note: The policy review recommended moving the pre-change review before the final plans notice (R-007). If the client adopts it, the pre-change review is due before the SCN-TRF-NFP date in the notices table

decisions_needed.question: Is CR-014 transformative or adaptive?
decisions_needed.reason: It adds a capability agencies configure and a new third party in the delivery path, which needs new MAS-CSO-TPR documentation and an assessment of the new flow. Choosing adaptive drops the 30 and 10 business day notices before the start

decisions_needed.question: Confirm the business day basis: Monday to Friday, skipping US federal holidays.
options: Also skip the client's own holidays (client supplies the dates)
decisions_needed.reason: FedRAMP does not define business days. Counting weekdays only would put the final plans notice on 2027-01-18, the Martin Luther King Jr. federal holiday; the default moves it to 2027-01-15

open_questions.question: Are the two pilot agencies using the offering, and what is the offering's FedRAMP ID?
open_questions.why: All necessary parties include any agency using the offering (FRD-ANP). The change log recorded on 2026-11-19 that no agency was relying on it

open_questions.question: Who approves CR-014 (name and title)?
open_questions.why: SCN-CSO-INF requires it in the notice

open_questions.question: Is there a security impact analysis for CR-014?
Which chat messaging service is T6, and what are its usage and configuration, justification, mitigation measures and compensating controls?
open_questions.why: MAS-CSO-TPR requires them before the scope log entry

open_questions.question: Which KSIs does the change affect, and how will they be validated?
open_questions.why: SCN-CSO-INF requires the plan for validating impacted KSIs. The SME identifies them from the change and the validator designs
